The test image shows a severely damaged tomato leaf with:
- Extensive yellow chlorosis
- Large brown necrotic lesion covering most of the leaf
- Leaf curling/rolling and desiccation
- Some dark spots on the remaining yellow-green tissue
- Brown petiole

Top candidates: Late Blight, Early Blight, Phytophthora Blight, Bacterial Canker, Septoria Leaf Blotch, Alternaria, Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus, Leaf Mold.

Now I'll view one reference per candidate class.

Having viewed all 8 reference images, here is my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Large irregular brown necrotic lesion covering most of the leaf
- Yellow chlorosis in remaining green portions
- Severe leaf curling/desiccation
- Some dark speckling on yellowed tissue
- Brown/desiccated petiole

**Comparison to references:**
- **Late Blight** (CDDM_498): Very close match — large brown necrotic area spreading across the leaf while remaining tissue yellows, same tan-brown color and desiccated texture
- **Early Blight** (CDDM_1107): Small circular target-spot lesions — does not match the large irregular necrosis
- **Phytophthora Blight** (Bugwood_21): Stem lesions, not leaf-dominant necrosis
- **Bacterial Canker** (Bugwood_4): Marginal yellowing and small dark spots — partial match but necrosis far less extensive
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch** (CDDM_1928): Small discrete circular spots on green leaf — no match
- **Alternaria** (Bugwood_4): Stem canker at soil line — no match
- **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus** (Bugwood_3): Whole-plant wilting/bronzing — no match
- **Leaf Mold** (CDDM_313): Pale diffuse spots — no match

The test image most closely resembles **Late Blight** — the large brown necrotic lesion with yellow chlorosis and desiccation is the hallmark presentation seen in the Late Blight reference.
